answer: One concrete sybil defense is a staked-identity graph: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before earning rewards, and each new identity is only credited after a peer attests it controls unique compute, like a falcon verifying territory before it hunts. A sybil attacker must pay the deposit for every fake cedar in the forest of accounts and burn compute proving each is distinct; because rewards scale with verified work rather than account count, cloning identities into shale-like layers of worthless duplicates costs more than any gain, so attackers lose capital on each clone created.
